same_change.instructions: You are shown two pull requests from the same repository, A and B. A and B make the same change: they fix the same problem or add the same thing in essentially the same way (one may be a slightly larger or later revision of the other), so merging both would be redundant.

same_goal.instructions: You are shown two pull requests from the same repository, A and B. A and B aim at the same goal: the same bug, issue, ticket or intended outcome, whether or not they take the same approach.

same_branch.instructions: You are shown two pull requests from the same repository, A and B. A and B target the same base branch or release line; answer low if one is a backport, cherry-pick or promotion of the work to another branch (for example main vs a release branch, or edge vs stable).

builds_on.instructions: You are shown two pull requests from the same repository, A and B. One of them builds on the other: it continues, extends, follows up, fixes, or reverts the other's change, so it only makes sense with the other in mind.
